On load, `AppProvider` (`src/app/provider.tsx`) wraps the whole app in `AuthLoader`, which comes from `configureAuth` in `src/lib/auth.tsx`. That calls `getUser`, which sends `GET /auth/me` through the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`, with credentials so the session cookie is sent. While that call is pending, `AuthLoader` shows a spinner. The result is cached by React Query as `useUser()`. `ProtectedRoute` in `src/lib/auth.tsx`, used in `src/app/router.tsx`, treats a missing `user.data` as signed out and renders `<Navigate>` to `/auth/login?redirectTo=<current path>`. `AuthLayout` (`src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx`) does the opposite on the sign-in and register pages: once `user.data` exists, it navigates to `redirectTo` or the dashboard.

Every failed request goes through the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. It first shows an error toast with the server's message, or the Axios message if the server sent none. Then, if the status is 401, it sets `window.location.href` to the login path, so the app does a full page load to sign-in. The `/auth/me` call on load goes through the same interceptor, so a signed-out visitor who opens any page is redirected to sign-in this way, and the toast still appears.

Reading the code, I found a bug in the 401 redirect. It builds `new URLSearchParams()` and reads `redirectTo` from that empty object, so it always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. Any query string on the page is lost. I did not run the app to confirm this. The fix is to read `window.location.search`, or to use the current `href`.
